Project Coordinator

Phoenix, AZ

The Project Coordinator partners with project managers and executives, property management and accounting teams, and general contractors to ensure the successful execution of development and construction projects.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Assist in monitoring and managing documentation flow and communications associated with development and construction projects of varying sizes.
Generate requests for bid packages, bid comparison documents, budgets, and schedules.
Develop and distribute meeting minutes and project report(s).
Administer contracts with all vendors.
Prepare monthly budget updates and monthly draw packages.
Manage construction document files and close out documentation.
Generate monthly fee billing for Lincoln.
Participate in internal and external development programs and mentoring to grow into advanced roles.
Contribute through thoughtful and proactive execution of clearly defined duties, methods, and tasks; contribute to team performance through suggestions to improve systems, processes, and procedures.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional administrative support experience, preferably focused on construction management or real estate
Intermediate skills with Microsoft Office Suite, including Power Point and Project required; Procore Construction Software preferred
Ability to effectively interact/communicate verbally and in writing with teammates and leadership team in a straightforward, professional manner, keeping the appropriate customer(s) informed/updated as needed
Ability to analyze and interpret commercial lease, architect and engineer consulting, and general contractor agreement as well as construction documentation
Ability to work independently and in a team setting, take direction from multiple Project Managers, and carry out tasks with little direction
Ability to effectively collaborate with internal and external Project Managers, architects, engineers, consultants, and general contractors, including the ability to give direction
Knowledge of financial terms and principles; ability to calculate figures such as percentages, discounts, markups, and/or commissions
Strong organizational skills with an inquisitive and entrepreneurial mindset
Proven track record of delivering excellent internal and external customer service
Ability to work after hours, weekends, holidays, and during emergency situations as necessary to meet the needs of the client
Ability to read and write English in order to understand manuals and procedures, and to write reports

Physical Requirements

Ability to sit/stand/walk for long periods of time, including walking unfinished construction project sites and on uneven surfaces; manual dexterity to operate a computer keyboard, phone, and other office equipment; eyesight that allows for reading a computer screen, phone screen, reports, etc.; hearing that allows for hearing/understanding spoken words; lifting and carrying up to 20 lbs.; tolerant of loud noises, airborne dust, chemicals, fumes, and inclement weather.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed above are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. This position is 100% in-office
. The role requires working in office during standard business hours. Remote work or telecommuting is not an option for this position.

JLL is seeking a Project Coordinator to support its Data Collection and Analytics (DCA) team—a fully self-performed field organization operating across more than 30 countries. As Project Coordinator, you will play a critical role in driving operational excellence by supporting administrative functions, coordinating project execution, and ensuring that critical deadlines are met in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment. Job Summary

The Program Coordinator for the Kinney Center for Interdisciplinary Renaissance Studies works with the Director and Librarian to manage and develop the Center’s research, educational, arts, and public facing programs.

Essential Functions

Identify, develop, and expand cross-institutional partnerships with educational and public art institutions by taking the lead on targeted outreach and program development. Meet with students, scholars, and administrators of other Renaissance Centers and scholarly programs.

Develop sustainable research partnerships with external Renaissance Centers.

Identify and research grant funding proposals on a regional and national level. Prepare, develop, and co-author, in collaboration with an interdisciplinary team of scholars, grant proposals and applications.

Steward designated financial resources of the Center toward mission goals.

Work collaboratively with Center staff, University Departments, and community organizations to identify and oversee the development of opportunities for new research networks, a wide range of educational opportunities, and public-facing arts projects that link the history, literature, and art of the Renaissance to modern times. Such projects include musical and theatrical performances; the expansion of the Renaissance of the Earth project across its educational, research, and public-facing agendas; development of new focus on questions of social and environmental justice; expanding undergraduate opportunities for interdisciplinary work-study.

Cultivate relationships with local artists, herbalists, farmers, and orchardists to expand and market the Renaissance of the Earth research project and Grounded Knowledge Workshops.

Design, implement, and publicize public-facing output (e.g. workshops, performances, arts, and rare book exhibitions, one day symposia on research themes) in consultation with faculty and graduate student research teams.

Organize an annual meeting of 5 College librarians and faculty to identify topics of interest for cross-institutional exhibits, develop question driven pathways through book exhibitions that connect to the learning objectives of 5 College course offerings. Work closely with special collections librarians to identify texts and material objects that can be used for educational purposes in workshop and classroom settings.

Develop an artist-in-residence program at the Kinney Center. Working closely with the Director, develop relationships with arts programs and centers on the east coast identifying opportunities for short-term and long-term artist in residence programs. This may include inviting musicians of historical music, actors, playwrights, directors, visual artists, and authors whose creative work draws upon or adapts questions from the Renaissance. Extend invitations to visual artists to produce gallery shows at Center, musicians to perform on the program’s outdoor stage, actors and dramaturgs to work together to develop new playscripts; as well as dance.

Work closely with invited guests to identify potential research and educational intersections between invitee and ongoing intellectual projects at center. Manage publicity for events via public posts, social media, and mailing lists. Coordinate room reservations, travel arrangements. Reserve appropriate University facilities for event use.

Create internship opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students across the 5 Colleges with an emphasis on the Renaissance of the Earth research project. In addition, identify internship opportunities for working with a rare book collection. Network with faculty across the 5 Colleges to identify students that will benefit the program. Expand the work-study offerings by developing new programming proposals for the Center.

Other Functions

Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in early modern literature, history, or related field.

At least two years of arts administration experience.

Knowledge of subject areas specific to the research mission of the Center including the history, culture, arts, and languages of the global Renaissance

Successful grant writing experience and knowledge of funding opportunities and strategies.

Familiarity with rare books and manuscripts and ability to read the roman, italic, and gothic typefaces that are most common in Renaissance print materials.

Ability to work collaboratively and foster an inclusive team environment, leveraging diverse perspectives from a wide variety of internal and external groups.

Experience advising executive staff on strategic matters.

Ability to take initiative, work independently, multi-task and meet deadlines.

Experience managing complex, highly visible projects.

Impeccable writing, editing, research, and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Typical office work environment.

Additional Details

Direct supervision received from the Kinney Center Director.

This position is subject to final budgetary and administrative approval.

Working Conditions

Work is primarily performed in an indoor university environment and involves lifting and transporting materials or equipment and general physical activity, including prolonged standing, walking, or assuming low postures.

Work Schedule and Work Arrangement

8:30 AM - 5:00 PM Monday - Friday, with occasional evenings and weekends for pre-scheduled events.

Job Description

Join the HJF Team!

HJF is seeking a Program Coordinator
with a scientific background to support the Scientific Project Management Branch within the Military Relevant Bacterial Diseases Department (MRBD) within the Infectious Diseases Directorate at the Naval Medical Research Command (NMRC) providing programmatic and administrative support to the Operationally Relevant Infections Department. The incumbent will coordinate budget and accounting, meetings management, project management, contracts, and purchasing. The incumbent will also complete more routine tasks independently as well as tasks delegated by Senior Program Manager.

This position will be in support of the MRBD Department at the NMRC. The NMRC is an agency that performs basic and applied biomedical research to meet the needs of the United States Navy and United States Marine Corps. Its areas of focus include study of infectious diseases, biodefense, military medicine, battlefield medicine, and bone marrow research. The NMRC laboratory is co-located in the Daniel K. Inouye Building with the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research at the U.S. Army Forest Glen Annex, Silver Spring, Maryland.

The newly established MRBD Department is built on the legacy of the former Enteric Disease and Wound Infection research departments of NMRC. The Enteric Diseases Division (EDD) and Combat Wound Infections (CWID) divisions of MRBD are dedicated to three main research goals: assessment, prevention and treatment of enteric and wound infections caused by bacterial pathogens of high military relevance.

The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals.

TELUS Digital AI Community

Our global AI Community is a vibrant network of more than one million contributors from diverse backgrounds who help customers collect, enhance, train, translate, and localize content to build better AI models. Your knowledge of USA's geography, local landmarks, and how people actually navigate your region is something no algorithm can fully replicate. •    Variety, not monotony: your day moves between sponsor relationships, logistics, operations, and finance; no two days look the same.

•    Comfort navigating patient, employee and client interactions, various billing workflows, claims and remittance, and collection processes.
•    Excel and Google Workspace skills adept enough to keep notes, logs and general work accurate and current.

new_jobs.title: Global Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Dermalogica continues to lead the professional skin care industry with distribution in over 80 countries. Known worldwide as the premiere Skin Therapist’s choice for offering the most respected professional skin care line, we are also recognized for our renowned postgraduate education.

Our entrepreneurial spirit, hands-on environment and fast-paced culture encourages employees to be their best, bringing innovative solutions to reach the skin care professional and consumer. We are highly energetic, passionate, and results oriented. You will find that Dermalogica is a very special place, with tremendous opportunities ahead for us, all building upon a record of achievement.

In 2015 Dermalogica was acquired by Unilever, one of the world’s largest and most successful consumer goods companies. While Dermalogica continues to operate as a stand-alone entrepreneurial business, we now have enviable access to cutting edge capabilities and resources to help us win in our markets.

The challenge is to build on the legacy of our brand, our experienced team and our industry leading education to deliver profitable growth. One of the key elements for our success, and critical for our growth, is bringing in the right people to join our team. We invite you to come and make a difference and grow your career with the global leader in skin care.

Global Data Analyst
– Role Description:

The Global Data Analyst takes ownership of Dermalogica’s Global and International reporting and analytics ecosystem across all markets and channels. This role is responsible for maintaining, enhancing and occasionally building dashboards in Tableau and Power BI, working with IT and the market teams to ensure data quality and accuracy across global sell-in and sell-out data sets. Success in this role means empowering stakeholders across the business with reliable, timely insights.

Our analytics agenda is moving at pace and this role is central to achieving our goal of industry-leading, globally consistent reporting. Key priorities include establishing a standard data model within a future-proofed environment, continuing to develop and consolidate analytic tools in Power BI, ensuring data integrity and governance across markets, and building analytical capability across the wider business. We need an inquisitive individual who can drive this agenda forward as our global footprint and channel mix continue to expand.

Key Job Responsibilities:

Ownership, Development & Maintenance of Reports & Dashboards (Power BI)
Own and maintain all global and international reports and data flows in Power BI – including proactive troubleshooting, validating data quality and accuracy, and updating dashboards with relevant new information (e.g. new innovations, markets, channels).
Ensure dashboards are kept up to date with manual data reports (such as Amazon US sell-out data, provided in an excel format). As part of this, review current distribution of reports in Excel and determine what can be simplified/automated in Power BI.
Take full ownership of sell-out data integrity and act as the primary bridge between business users and IT for sell-in data queries. Drive ongoing simplification and process streamlining across all reporting.
Provide ad hoc analytical support for global departments, market GMs and senior leadership, responding to dashboard queries and delivering timely, accurate data across markets and channels.
Ensure global and regional departments have standardized, user-friendly analytical tools and dashboards for self-sufficient performance management – including monitoring usage, retiring unused workbooks, and keeping all reports accessible in the proper formats.
Design and build new Power BI dashboards end-to-end – from data engineering and modelling through to visualization – with a focus on question-led, actionable insights and performance benchmarking (vs. target, vs. prior year, vs. market).

Data Analytics
Provide monthly innovation tracking updates across markets as input to global performance calls, analyzing launch performance vs. expectations and identifying trends by region and channel.
Build analytical models to assess how new business opportunities impact existing channels across markets, highlighting potential risk factors and identifying growth opportunities based on cross-market performance and sister brand insights

Experience and Competencies Required:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Science, Business Analytics or another related field.
3-5 years of previous analytical experience
Proficient in SQL, Power BI, and Excel, with hands-on experience building visualizations from large data sets and multiple data sources. Additional BI/ETL tools, automation skills (Python, Power Automate), or programming knowledge are a plus.
Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and highly organized with a willingness to learn autonomously
Tech savvy with an open mindset about learning new technologies, systems, and tools
Strong ownership mindset with excellent initiative and follow-through; a track record of proactively identifying opportunities and driving end-to-end solutions in a fast-paced environment
Analytical mindset with the ability to dive deep into complex, ambiguous problems, perform root cause analysis, and ask the right questions to deliver solution-focused outcomes
Courage to challenge established norms in a constructive way and drive change

The expected base salary range for this position is $80K to $100K. The exact base salary is determined by various factors including experience, skills, education, and budget. This position is also eligible for participation in the company discretionary bonus plan, based on personal performance and company results.

The role will be based out of the corporate headquarters in Carson, Los Angeles. It will be hybrid with applicable on-site work guidelines.

Student visas and H1B sponsorships will not be considered at this time.

Apply now and become a team member for the preeminent global leader in skincare providing a competitive and comprehensive health benefits package including life/accident/disability insurance, wellness programs, paid family leave, domestic partner benefits, education/training programs, product allowances, fitness reimbursement, 401(k) matching, and a host of other great perks.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP currently has opportunities for On-Call Archaeology Field Technicians for project work in California. Selected applicants will primarily monitor construction projects with our Earth & Environment Cultural Resource Team and will have open opportunities to become part of a growing organization that meets our client’s objectives and solves their cultural resource challenges. This On-Call Archaeology Field Technician position will work with supervisory field staff and senior archaeologists to complete assigned fieldwork tasks (primarily monitoring, survey, testing, and data recovery). Compensation will be commensurate with credentials and experience.

Current project contributions are needed in Southern California; however, the successful candidate should expect upcoming or future fieldwork opportunities in adjacent states including Nevada and Arizona. The positions are expected to take active roles in conducting monitoring and survey fieldwork and supporting field data collection. The successful candidate will have experience with various digital data collection software (such as ESRI FieldMaps, Survey 123, and WildNote) and would be expected to contribute to the completion of state DPR-523 forms.

Your Impact

Participation in cultural resource monitoring during preconstruction and construction activities.
Participating in and/or contributing to cultural resource investigations in support of our clients’ projects. These efforts require compliance with NEPA, NHPA, NAGPRA, and other federal, state and local laws and regulations.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

BA/BS degree (MS/MA preferred) in anthropology, archaeology, historical archaeology
1-3 years related archaeological field experience in California
Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work in a team environment, and excellent oral and written communication skills.
Working knowledge of cultural resources and environmental regulations and North American archaeology including Southern California, Mojave Desert, and Great Basin.
Experience with ESRI FieldMaps.
Experience with NHPA, ARPA, NAGPRA, and relevant state laws.
Ability to perform pedestrian survey and carry up to 25 lbs. of personal gear and company equipment.
Ability to perform archaeological fieldwork (survey, monitoring) in hot, dry high-desert conditions.
Experience identifying and analyzing a wide variety of archaeological materials from prehistoric and historic-period archaeological sites in the field.
Must be willing to travel to a remote project location for up to 10-day rotations.
Willing travel to project site in Southern California. Per diem provided.

Preferred Qualifications:

Previous work experience in California, Great Basin, or Southwest United States.
Large scale construction monitoring and/or terrestrial survey project experience is a plus.

WSP Benefits:

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on a providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation:

Expected Salary: $ 26.00 - $39.62 per hour

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

new_jobs.description:
About Us

The California Institute for Behavioral Health Solutions (CIBHS) is a statewide nonprofit dedicated to strengthening behavioral health systems and improving outcomes for individuals, families, and communities in California and beyond. We operate at the intersection of clinical expertise and systems transformation, advancing behavioral health through a comprehensive ecosystem of technical expertise that blends implementation science and evidence-based practices with community-defined approaches to deliver sustainable, scalable solutions grounded in real-world needs. Bridging policy and practice, CIBHS partners with state and local agencies, providers, and community organizations to deliver expert training, technical assistance and capacity building; and third-party administration services.

Position Overview

CIBHS is seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Senior Project Coordinator to support the administration and implementation of complex grant-funded behavioral health initiatives that serve communities across California. 

This position will play a key role in coordinating and supporting day-to-day activities of the Community‑Defined Behavioral Health Initiative (CDBHI) grant program, and the execution of the CDBHI project communications plan. Day-to-day activities include monitoring, tracking, calendaring, meeting preparation and documentation, developing marketing materials and digital content, and managing registrations for program trainings and events. In this role, the Senior Project Coordinator will work closely with the Communications team and other internal teams, consultants, partners, funders, and clients to help ensure work is organized, timely, well-documented, and aligned with program goals and funding requirements.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys managing details, coordinating multiple moving pieces, communicating with diverse stakeholders, and supporting mission-driven projects that improve behavioral health systems and services.

Key Responsibilities

Plan and coordinate logistics for meetings, workshops, webinars, trainings, and other project‑related events.

Demonstrated ability to coordinate timelines, logistics, documentation, and deliverables with strong attention to detail.

Strong proofreading, editing, written communication, and verbal communication skills.

Excellent organizational, time management, problem-solving, and follow-through skills.

Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel.

new_jobs.description:
Overview

We are hiring! We are seeking an energetic, highly motivated, and detail-oriented self-starter to join our geospatial team as a Senior
GIS Analyst
in our Ft. Lauderdale
office. Our ideal candidate will have education and experience with geospatial analysis, mapping processes, GIS software and technologies.

Under supervision, performs standard geographic information system (GIS) work while developing professional proficiency. Will work with an interdisciplinary group of GIS analysts, developers, and project managers out of client offices in Ft. Lauderdale (not remote).

Your role

Assist the Program Services section with the administration and maintenance of on premises ArcGIS Enterprise and ArcGIS Online.
Serve as the point of contact for various GIS projects/assignments.
Assist the Program Services section with maintaining the GIS applications, servers, layers, and feature classes for all FDOT District Four offices.
Attend requirement gathering and GIS coordination meetings.
Define project tasks and execute on those tasks.
Work with existing ArcGIS databases, datasets and applications to develop an understanding of their use and integration capabilities.
Develop solutions to ArcGIS needs using a combination of tools including app builders (ArcGIS Instant Apps, ArcGIS Dashboards, ArcGIS StoryMaps, and ArcGIS Experience Builder).
Work with FDOT ArcGIS Users developers, etc. to understand data landscape and needs.
Conducts data gathering, conversion and analysis of GIS data, prepares data documentation or metadata for GIS Projects, prepares maps and exhibits with GIS data sets, and participates in client needs analyses.
Maintains continued knowledge of technology developments in the GIS field and use of GIS software.
Performs such other duties as the Supervisor may from time to time deem necessary.
Write clear technical documentation to support data development work.
Collaborate with technical and nontechnical staff to understand client GIS needs .

new_jobs.title: Business Development GIS Analyst
new_jobs.description:
At Devon, we will offer you a career full of energy and unmatched opportunities to solve today’s greatest challenges. Innovation, creative problem-solving and positive change happen when people step out of their comfort zone and think differently. Our values, workplace practices, wellness programs, benefits and compensation are aimed at helping employees manage their unique personal life and care for their families so they can focus on contributing to the fullest.

Job Profile Summary

Primary responsibility is to contribute to Corporate Asset Evaluation Team (“AET”) with a focus on Acquisitions & Divestitures and other project-based evaluations. The role focuses on GIS, spatial analysis, data integration, and workflow automation to support asset evaluations and business decisions.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Gather, analyze, and integrate sub-surface data into spatial workflows for asset evaluations.
Interface with geologic, well attribute, economic, and ownership data.
Perform geospatial analysis including spatial joins, dissolves, table joins/relates, georeferencing, proximity analysis, and spatial calculations.
Develop and maintain GIS models, scripts, and automated workflows.
Maintain geospatial data quality and integrity within an enterprise environment.
Digitize and maintain oil & gas leases, competitor acreage, DSUs, development units, and other relevant spatial features.
Calculate PDP well spacing and support development inventory generation.
Integrate well, inventory, Enverus, vendor, and internal datasets into GIS workflows.
Integrate economic information with sub-surface attributes into visual products for executive and board-of-director-level presentations.
Create maps, analytical products, and presentation-ready displays supporting AET technical screenings and evaluations.
Support rapid-turnaround data-room evaluations and other A&D activities.
Identify opportunities to improve and automate AET data and GIS workflows.

Skills And Experience

+5 years’ experience of GIS or related fields.
Familiar with A&D processes.
Strong proficiency with ArcGIS Pro and Esri enterprise GIS environments.
Familiarity with FME Workbench.
Experience with geoprocessing, spatial analysis, and workflow automation using ArcGIS, FME, Python, or similar tools.
Experience with SQL, relational databases, and integration of large spatial datasets.
Experience publishing map services, feature layers, configuring web apps, and using ArcGIS Experience Builder.
Experience with raster data, aerial imagery, and LiDAR is a plus.
Experience with Kingdom, Spotfire, FME, Petrel, Enverus, or similar upstream technical platforms is a plus.
Strong problem-solving, communication, and organizational skills.
Ability to deliver high-quality work on short timelines in a fast-paced A&D environment.
Oil & gas E&P experience or industry knowledge strongly preferred.

Education

Bachelors degree in related field is preferred.

new_jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
new_jobs.description:
About Us

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. As part of our team, you’ll discover a world of opportunities to connect with innovative thinkers, forge your path, and have fun tackling the world’s most challenging projects. At TRC, Member of WSP, you can have a rewarding career on every level.

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

Overview

TRC is seeking an Entry Level Environmental Scientist to join our Windsor, CT Engineering, Construction, and Remediation team. This position would be part of a very skilled team that works closely with Project Managers and other technical leads providing technical support for site investigation, due diligence, groundwater monitoring, remediation, and regulatory compliance projects. We are looking for an enthusiastic, flexible, and personable individual with an eye for detail, a willingness to learn, and a desire to be part of a growing and high performing team.

Responsibilities

Support environmental compliance and remediation related projects in the field and office.
Perform a variety of field work including environmental assessments, environmental investigations, soil and groundwater sampling, site inspections, and subcontractor oversight.
Prepare and review technical reports, feasibility studies, work plans, design documents, and construction documents in support of engineering design from pilot to full-scale remediation system design.
Support management of medium-to-large, complex tasks to ensure internal and external expectations are met for scope, budget, schedule, and quality.
Assist during proposal development including preparation of work scopes and budgets.
Limited travel regionally and state-wide on short and long-term assignments.

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in Environmental Science, Geoscience or Geology from an accredited university.
Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite.
Excellent attitude and ability to work well within a team environment.
Excellent writing/verbal communication skills for interaction with multi-disciplinary staff, clients, and regulatory agencies.
Ability (with training) to perform and manage field work (construction oversight, drilling oversight, soil/groundwater sampling, etc.).
Must be able to pass a pre-employment drug screen, background check and motor vehicle records check.
Valid Driver’s License is required.
Knowledge of AutoCAD, MicroStation, ESRI, and/or HydroCAD.
0-1 year or Internship experience in the field of environmental compliance or groundwater remediation consulting preferred
40-hour HAZWOPER health and safety training certificate (with an up-to-date 8-hr annual refresher course certification).
Knowledge of environmental regulations (NJDEP)

Benefits*: TRC offers a competitive benefit package consisting of:

Medical, dental, vision, and disability insurance.
401k package that includes both traditional and Roth IRA options and Company match.
Paid time off contingent upon full time or part time status and level of seniority (ranging from 15 to 25 days per year).
All full-time employees enjoy a minimum of 8 Paid Holidays per year.
TRC ensures that all employees, including those that work part-time, receive paid sick, family, and disability leave in accordance with the laws of their state of residence.
These benefits are applicable to US employees depending on their employment status (full time, part time, or temporary). TRC offers jurisdiction specific benefit packages for International and Puerto Rico employees.

Compensation: In accordance with local law, the below salary range is applicable for the job and location associated with this requisition. Compensation will vary based upon experience, education, skill level, geographical location, and other compensable factors.

Other Compensation: Employee may be eligible for participation in the Company’s annual Discretionary Bonus Program which is contingent on Company, Business Segment, and Individual performance against Key Performance Indicators which vary by year and employee.

Disclaimers

TRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

The complete job description and application are available on TRC’s career site.

TRC accepts applications for this position on an ongoing, rolling basis and reserves the right to cancel this posting at any time.

Would you like to have a career with a collaborative, diverse, and dynamic mining company? We have an exciting opportunity for you!

new_jobs.title: Data Analyst - GEOINT SME
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Everforth ECS is seeking a Data Analyst, GEOINT Technical Subject Matter Expert (SME)
, to work at our St. Louis, MO
customer site.

Note: This position is contingent upon contract award and final acceptance by government customer.

Data Analyst - GEOINT Technical SME Work Role

Everforth ECS is seeking a Data Analyst GEOINT SME that encompasses a comprehensive skill set focused on leveraging data to enhance organizational performance, ensure security, and drive strategic decisions. This includes the technical depth of integrating, developing, and maintaining analytic models, visualizations, and tools specifically designed to deter, detect, and mitigate insider threats by identifying anomalous events. A core function is the application of industry-standard data science principles to develop and sustain risk scoring tools and other data analytics implementations while supporting system integrity by capturing and analyzing metrics on system errors, failures, and data transfers. Complementing this technical expertise is the breadth of business analysis, which involves collaborating with project requesters, stakeholders, and managers to refine project requests and clarify business objectives. These professionals use data analytics to derive actionable business insights, draw logical conclusions, develop forecasts, identify organizational inefficiencies, and ultimately recommend and implement strategies to improve overall performance.

Duties May Include

Data Analysis and Visualization: Develop data analytics and visualizations by applying proven, industry-standard data science principles and techniques. Create and edit visual content, including charts, graphs, and dashboards, to transform quantitative and qualitative datasets into compelling, understandable visuals.
Business Process Improvement: Collaborate with project requestors, stakeholders, and project managers to refine project requests and clarify business needs and objectives. Use data analytics to form business insights, identify issues, and recommend effective ways to boost organizational efficiency.
Analytical Model Support: Integrate, develop, and maintain analytic models, visualizations, and tools designed to deter, detect, and mitigate insider threats. Support the sustainment of risk scoring tools and other data analysis implementations by identifying and helping to resolve system errors and failures.
Stakeholder Collaboration: Work closely with subject matter experts to learn about specific products and processes. Support the preparation of reports and briefs on analyses and dashboard functionality for various internal teams.
Data and Metrics Management: Capture, maintain, and accumulate statistics that show quantities and timelines for key processes, such as data transfers between domains, to support system integrity and performance monitoring.
Policy and Communications Support: Assist in supporting Policy Business Operations, including policy development, review, and coordination. Contribute to the creation and revision of technical documents, reports, and communications materials, ensuring they convey a consistent message.
Other Duties as assigned.

Salary Range: $110,000-135,000

Benefits

General Description of Benefits

Required Skills

U.S. Citizenship
Bachelor’s Degree in Data Science, Statistics, Business, or a related field
Active TS/SCI with ability to pass CI Poly
At least 12 months demonstrated experience in one or more Geospatial Information Systems tools such as ArcView, ArcGIS, Remote View, ArcIMS, ERDAS Imagine, Remote View, ERDAS Imagine, Macromedia Dreamweaver, Macromedia Fireworks, Photoshop, HTML, and FrameMaker
Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, with a proven ability to weigh the relative costs and benefits of potential actions and identify the most appropriate solution
Highly developed interpersonal and oral/written communication skills, with the ability to effectively and professionally interact with a diverse set of stakeholders (from peers to end-users to executive management)
Demonstrated ability to use data to form business insights, draw logical conclusions, and contribute to performance-improving strategies
Experience in collaborating with stakeholders to clarify project needs and business objectives
Familiarity with the concepts of analytical model development and maintenance
Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment
Proficiency in creating and editing visual content such as charts and graphs to represent data
Demonstrated coding experience to support writing scripts with tools such as, but not limited to, Java and Python
Demonstrated ability to use SharePoint, Tableau, Redmine, and other systems/databases to manipulate and build data visualizations

Desired Skills

Active TS/SCI w/CI Poly
Experience supporting insider threat, risk scoring, or similar security-focused analytics programs
Experience with policy development or process improvement initiatives
Familiarity with GEOINT analysis software or NGA-specific applications

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Join the HJF Team!

HJF is seeking a Data Analyst II
to provide analytic support to epidemiologists, biostatisticians and scientists and ensure data quality and data integrity.

This hybrid position supports the work of the Divisions of Military Child and Family Research and Health Systems Research and Clinical Epidemiology in the Department of Pediatrics at the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences in Bethesda, MD.

The Data Analyst II will be responsible for data extraction, management, cleaning and analysis associated with pediatric research projects drawing upon military healthcare data, and will support other Pediatric projects as needed. The successful candidate will collaborate with principal investigators, epidemiologists, and other data analysts and managers to establish data requirements. They will structure, manipulate and clean and analyze data to meet research needs in SAS. Data quality control, data updates and merges, statistics, data queries, streamlining/ developing efficiencies for data processes, regulatory oversight, and scientific graphics are all key tasks. This position reports to Principal Investigators and receives daily supervision from team Epidemiologists. This is the second of three levels in the Data Analyst hierarchy.

The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals.

Responsibilities

Writes SAS programs for data extraction, cleaning, structuring, validation, and analysis, as well as preparing data for presentation and publication to support the work of Principal Investigators.
Recommends operating methods to improve processing, distribution, data flow, collection and database editing procedures.
Ensures data quality through:
Making recommendations concerning the outline of data requirements and data structuring based on research goals in consultation with project leaders and end users.
Testing data to identify integrity, validity and quality issues.
Troubleshooting problems concerning database records.
Communicating and discussing solutions-oriented recommendations to co-workers and end users.

Provides knowledge management through:
Assisting investigators in preparation of results for presentation.
Documenting methods and outcomes for use by the research team.
Contributing to writing of research reports and scientific publications as requested, with particular focus on methods and results.
Supporting drafting of elements of research grants, protocols, and data sharing agreement documentation.

Maintains subject matter expertise through a current working knowledge of all military health system data systems and resources to advise Investigators on appropriate data for their research goals.
Develops knowledge and skills in research design and data analysis to best answer questions of interest that advance the work of the group. Assists in making data from MHS databases and other data sources accessible to researchers and other users to answer research questions of importance.
Ensures compliance with regulatory and ethical requirements for data security during human subjects’ data acquisition, transfer, storage, analysis and archiving.
Provides assistance and training to new research team employees or research personnel when new protocols begin or as new data extraction or analysis work is needed.
May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the supervisor. This may include attendance of and participation in required training for the role.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

Bachelor's Degree Required; Master’s Degree Preferred
Minimum of 3-5 years experience required

Required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Must have strong SAS skills.
Demonstrated statistical and analytical experience, skills and passion for analyzing data including logistic, linear, and Poisson regression modeling. Other modeling experience such as hazards regression, GEE, etc would be a plus.
Knowledge and application of data cleansing and migration techniques.
Ability to investigate data issues and participate in remediation activities.
Ability to review detailed documents to validate data in operating systems.
Experience and willingness to write up methods and results, and perform data visualization.
The following are not required but are highly valued:
Knowledge of R, Python and/or ArcGIS software.
Familiarity with ICD-9 and ICD-10 coding.
Familiarity with or some experience with qualitative analysis methods.

Ability to obtain and maintain a T1 Public Trust background check.

Physical Capabilities

Ability to stand or sit at a computer for prolonged periods

Work Environment

This position will take place primarily in an office or clinic environment.

Compensation

The annual salary range for this position is $67,500-$78,000. Actual salary will be determined based on experience, education, etc.

Benefits

HJF offers a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on your health and well-being, from medical, dental, and vision coverage to health savings and retirement plans, and more.

Employment with HJF is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, which may include, but is not limited to, contacting your professional references, verification of previous employment, education and credentials, a criminal background check, and a department of motor vehicle (DMV) check if applicable. Reviews and signs off on draft and final reports, evaluations, and calculations for compliance with federal, state, and local regulations.
Ensures that firm policies and practices are followed on all assessments.

Collaborates with sales staff to create proposals in response to current and potential client requests for proposal (RFPs).

to improve the visibility of the firm's products and services in collaboration with applicable sales staff.
Provides technical guidance and training to more junior staff.
Mentors more junior staff and develops them for future growth within the discipline and firm.
May supervise the work of junior staff on project work.
Performs other duties as required.

Expert Knowledge of computer assisted design and drafting (CADD) 3D and 4D software and practices.
Expert knowledge of scientific methods and processes.
Expert Knowledge of Microsoft business software (excel, word, etc.).
Excellent verbal and written communications skills. Expert knowledge of federal, state and local regulations.

Bachelor's degree in Science or related discipline.
Registration as a licensed Professional Geologist, as certified by ASBOG.
7 years of related experience.

new_jobs.title: Data Analyst - Disaster Recovery Cadre
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding experienced Cost Estimators to our Disaster Recovery team to support current and future disaster recovery operations across the United States.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world's most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential - join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.
Support development of FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF) analyses when required.
Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in construction estimating, engineering, architecture, construction management, infrastructure planning, or a related discipline.
Experience developing conceptual, parametric, and detailed cost estimates for infrastructure or facility projects.
Experience estimating labor, equipment, material, and construction costs.
Familiarity with modern construction practices, facility assessments, project scope development, and construction inspection activities.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for field assignments.
Valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance regulations, policy, eligibility requirements, and the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG).
Previous FEMA experience as a Cost Estimator, Program Delivery Manager, Site Inspector, Hazard Mitigation Specialist, Policy Advisor, or similar disaster recovery role.
Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Physical Requirements

Ability to perform field inspections and site visits at disaster-impacted facilities and infrastructure when required by an assignment.
Ability to travel to client offices, applicant facilities, disaster recovery operation centers, and other project locations as needed.
Ability to perform computer-based estimating and technical review activities for extended periods during remote or office-based assignments.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Work assignments may be performed remotely, in the field, or through a hybrid arrangement depending on client needs and project requirements.
Field assignments may take place in disaster-impacted communities and at damaged public facilities or infrastructure sites.
Work conditions and location may vary by assignment, including active disaster recovery operations and geographically dispersed project teams.

Additional Information

This is an on-call, as-needed cadre position. Work assignments are not guaranteed and depend on disaster declarations, contract awards, client needs, project requirements, qualifications, availability, and recovery program activations.
Acceptance of assignments is voluntary, and periods of inactivity between deployments may occur.
Assignment schedules may be flexible and may include periods of high-intensity workload during active recovery operations.
Some deployments may require extended travel or mobilization on short notice; other assignments may be fully remote.
Evening and weekend work may be required during surge events or active disaster recovery operations.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 30,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor and we request priority referral of veterans.

We invite applications from all interested parties.

Explore our open positions at https://www.tetratech.com/careers. Follow us on social media to learn more about our people, culture, and opportunities:

LinkedIn: @TetraTechCareers

X (Twitter): @TetraTechJobs

Local contacts within the industry.
PG or applicable professional certification.
40-Hour OSHA Health & Safety Training (HAZWOPER) (29 CFR 1910.120).
Basic First Aid and Adult CPR.

CoAd helps businesses navigate the complexities of workforce management through a combination of technology, expertise, and human support. Serving more than 17,000 clients nationwide, CoAd delivers payroll, HR, benefits administration, compliance support, workforce technology, and PEO services that help organizations simplify operations, support their employees, and drive growth.

The Data Analyst, Customer Lifecycle Reporting owns performance reporting for the customer-facing functions in the Service organization. This role turns defined performance metrics into live Power BI reporting and, where an underlying data source does not yet exist, partners with the owning function to establish the instrumentation required to make the metric reportable. All work is built against a shared, reusable Power BI semantic model rather than one-off reports, so that each metric added lowers the cost of the next.

Key Responsibilities

Design, build, and maintain Power BI dashboards and executive scorecards for the Customer Lifecycle metric portfolio, built against the team's shared semantic model.
Create and maintain a prioritized delivery roadmap, sequencing work by executive value, data readiness, and implementation effort.

Support formal validation and sign-off of metric definitions and data sources as they move from draft to certified status.
Ensure data quality, consistency, and governance across assigned reporting.
Partner with functional leaders — the Head of Implementation (Client Activation) and the Head of Service (Customer Engagement, Customer Enablement, Customer Growth) — and report through to the COO on prioritization, to translate metrics into actionable insight.
Leverage AI tools to improve reporting, analysis, and automation.

Required Skills & Experience

3+ years of experience in data analytics, BI, or operations reporting (mid-level role — this work requires navigating undefined data sources and cross-functional coordination, not just building against clean data).
Hands-on experience with Power BI (data modeling, DAX, semantic models) and SQL.
Experience working directly with business stakeholders to define metrics and resolve data-quality or data-availability gaps.
Comfort operating inside a formal metric governance process (definitions, validation, sign-off) rather than ad hoc reporting requests.

The Business Data Analyst turns operational and product data into clear analysis that guides product decisions, improves business performance, and exposes opportunities for automation. The role works across structured warehouse data, event streams, and business systems to define metrics and explain what is driving changes in performance.

new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

As a Utility Network GIS Consultant, Manager, you will play a pivotal role in helping clients optimize operational efficiency through business application consulting. You will focus on utilizing Esri's software suite, such as ArcGIS, to analyze, manage, and visualize geographic data across various fields including urban planning, environmental management, and transportation. Within our Technology Consulting practice, you will be instrumental in implementing software solutions and providing training and support for seamless integration, enabling clients to achieve their strategic objectives.

As a Manager, you will enhance your leadership style by motivating, developing, and inspiring others to deliver quality. You are responsible for coaching, leveraging team members' unique strengths, and managing performance to meet client expectations. You are expected to lead with integrity and authenticity, articulating our purpose and values meaningfully. Embracing technology and innovation, you will enhance delivery and encourage others to do the same. In this role at PwC, you will take ownership of projects, confirming their successful planning, budgeting, execution, and completion, while addressing conflicts or issues and engaging in difficult conversations with clients and stakeholders.

Responsibilities

Leading the implementation and integration of Esri's software suite to optimize operational efficiency for clients
Analyzing geographic data to support urban planning, environmental management, and transportation projects
Managing client service accounts and driving engagement workstreams by supervising teams and solving complex problems
Developing and coaching team members to leverage their strengths and deliver quality outcomes
Utilizing Geographic Information System (GIS) applications and architecture to enhance data visualization and management
Taking ownership of projects, including planning, budgeting, execution, and completion
Encouraging innovation and embracing technology to improve service delivery and client satisfaction
Addressing conflicts and engaging in difficult conversations with stakeholders to maintain project alignment
Upholding professional and technical standards, including PwC's code of conduct and independence requirements
Building relationships with clients and team members to foster collaboration and strategic questioning

What You Must Have

At least a Bachelor's degree
At least 4 years of experience

What Sets You Apart

Preference for a Master's of Business Administration or PHD degree in at least one of the following fields of study: Computer and Information Science, Computer Engineering, Computer Management, Computer Science, Engineering, Geography, Geological Engineering, Geophysics, Information Technology, Management Information Systems
Utilizing Esri Mapping Software for advanced GIS applications
Demonstrating strategic questioning to drive project success
Embracing change and innovation in technology consulting
Developing skills in GIS architecture and conversion
Excelling in analytical thinking and problem-solving
Mentoring teams to enhance performance and deliver quality

new_jobs.title: Project Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Back to jobs

Project Coordinator

Phoenix, AZ

The Project Coordinator partners with project managers and executives, property management and accounting teams, and general contractors to ensure the successful execution of development and construction projects.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Assist in monitoring and managing documentation flow and communications associated with development and construction projects of varying sizes.
Generate requests for bid packages, bid comparison documents, budgets, and schedules.
Develop and distribute meeting minutes and project report(s).
Administer contracts with all vendors.
Prepare monthly budget updates and monthly draw packages.
Manage construction document files and close out documentation.
Generate monthly fee billing for Lincoln.
Participate in internal and external development programs and mentoring to grow into advanced roles.
Contribute through thoughtful and proactive execution of clearly defined duties, methods, and tasks; contribute to team performance through suggestions to improve systems, processes, and procedures.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional administrative support experience, preferably focused on construction management or real estate
Intermediate skills with Microsoft Office Suite, including Power Point and Project required; Procore Construction Software preferred
Ability to effectively interact/communicate verbally and in writing with teammates and leadership team in a straightforward, professional manner, keeping the appropriate customer(s) informed/updated as needed
Ability to analyze and interpret commercial lease, architect and engineer consulting, and general contractor agreement as well as construction documentation
Ability to work independently and in a team setting, take direction from multiple Project Managers, and carry out tasks with little direction
Ability to effectively collaborate with internal and external Project Managers, architects, engineers, consultants, and general contractors, including the ability to give direction
Knowledge of financial terms and principles; ability to calculate figures such as percentages, discounts, markups, and/or commissions
Strong organizational skills with an inquisitive and entrepreneurial mindset
Proven track record of delivering excellent internal and external customer service
Ability to work after hours, weekends, holidays, and during emergency situations as necessary to meet the needs of the client

The Program Coordinator for the Kinney Center for Interdisciplinary Renaissance Studies works with the Director and Librarian to manage and develop the Center’s research, educational, arts, and public facing programs.

Identify, develop, and expand cross-institutional partnerships with educational and public art institutions by taking the lead on targeted outreach and program development. Meet with students, scholars, and administrators of other Renaissance Centers and scholarly programs.

Develop sustainable research partnerships with external Renaissance Centers.

Identify and research grant funding proposals on a regional and national level. Prepare, develop, and co-author, in collaboration with an interdisciplinary team of scholars, grant proposals and applications.

Steward designated financial resources of the Center toward mission goals.

Work collaboratively with Center staff, University Departments, and community organizations to identify and oversee the development of opportunities for new research networks, a wide range of educational opportunities, and public-facing arts projects that link the history, literature, and art of the Renaissance to modern times. Work closely with special collections librarians to identify texts and material objects that can be used for educational purposes in workshop and classroom settings.

Develop an artist-in-residence program at the Kinney Center. Working closely with the Director, develop relationships with arts programs and centers on the east coast identifying opportunities for short-term and long-term artist in residence programs. Create internship opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students across the 5 Colleges with an emphasis on the Renaissance of the Earth research project. Expand the work-study offerings by developing new programming proposals for the Center.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Join the HJF Team!

HJF is seeking a Program Coordinator
with a scientific background to support the Scientific Project Management Branch within the Military Relevant Bacterial Diseases Department (MRBD) within the Infectious Diseases Directorate at the Naval Medical Research Command (NMRC) providing programmatic and administrative support to the Operationally Relevant Infections Department. The incumbent will coordinate budget and accounting, meetings management, project management, contracts, and purchasing. The incumbent will also complete more routine tasks independently as well as tasks delegated by Senior Program Manager.

This position will be in support of the MRBD Department at the NMRC. The NMRC is an agency that performs basic and applied biomedical research to meet the needs of the United States Navy and United States Marine Corps. Its areas of focus include study of infectious diseases, biodefense, military medicine, battlefield medicine, and bone marrow research. The NMRC laboratory is co-located in the Daniel K. Inouye Building with the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research at the U.S. Army Forest Glen Annex, Silver Spring, Maryland.

The newly established MRBD Department is built on the legacy of the former Enteric Disease and Wound Infection research departments of NMRC. The Enteric Diseases Division (EDD) and Combat Wound Infections (CWID) divisions of MRBD are dedicated to three main research goals: assessment, prevention and treatment of enteric and wound infections caused by bacterial pathogens of high military relevance.

The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals.

Responsibilities

Under supervision, ensures the terms and conditions of the award/ funding vehicle are adhered. Assists in ensuring all required reports are completed and submitted on time.

Provides administrative support under the direction of a supervisor such as hiring, purchasing, and tracking progress.
Assists in overseeing and managing collection, maintenance, analysis, and evaluation of data used in grant submissions, presentations, and publications.
May include budgetary responsibility to include plan/forecast.
May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the supervisor. This may include attendance of and participation in required training for role.

Bachelor's Degree in scientific field required.
Minimum of 0-2 years experience required.

Required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of organizational objectives, the federal budget process, office automation.
Ability to work completely independently, use sound judgement in solving problems.
Coordinate many complex systems and programs simultaneously.
Knowledge of project management principles, and good communications skills.
May require US Citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain T3/Secret Clearance.

Physical Capabilities

Ability to stand or sit at a computer for prolonged periods.

Work Environment

This position will take place primarily in an office setting.

The annual salary range for this position is $52,800-$65,000. Actual salary will be determined based on experience, education, etc.

HJF offers a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on your health and well-being, from medical, dental, and vision coverage to health savings and retirement plans, and more.

Employment with HJF is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, which may include, but is not limited to, contacting your professional references, verification of previous employment, education and credentials, a criminal background check, and a department of motor vehicle (DMV) check if applicable.
